root.name: Sicilian Defense: Euwe Attack, Prins Gambit

overview: White answers 2...d5 with 3.Bb2, leaving the e4 pawn en prise to ...dxe4. White hopes for a lead in development and long-diagonal pressure along the b2 bishop for the pawn. Black can take and hold the pawn, so the line is an offbeat gambit.

white_ideas.idea: Regain e4 with Nc3 and Bxe4-type play, using the Bb2 diagonal
Develop quickly with Nf3, Bb5+ and castle

black_ideas.idea: Take with 3...dxe4 and hold the pawn with ...Nf6 or ...Nc6
Develop and use the c5/d4 break

typical_structures.structure: White Bb2 on the long diagonal against e5/g7

character.notes: Open lines and a pawn deficit give White practical tricks but also danger.

gambit.notes: 3...dxe4 grabs a pawn Black can keep.

soundness.notes: Compensation is doubtful because Black has an easy development.

structure.notes: The e- and d-pawns trade, opening the centre.

sublines_that_differ.name: Black plays 3...d4
sublines_that_differ.how: No material is offered and the centre closes.

character.reason: White is a pawn down for development, which asks for sharp play.

gambit.reason: White leaves e4 to be taken in return for time.

soundness.reason: Black can accept with a clean structure, so the gambit scores on surprise.

structure.reason: Pawn trades in the centre open the lines for the bishops.

approach.reason: It is seldom played by strong players.

level.reason: Dubious lines cannot be Beginner and there is little to memorise.

plans.reason: The gambit is paid for with time and the b2 bishop.
